<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Rarely, users may wish to use DNS resolvers that do not operate on port 53. Typically this will be when users run a DNS resolver at home such as adguard or pihole and DNS redirection which may interfere with the response value from DNS IP. The is especially pertinent when calling the default hostname `myip.opendns.com` where both the actual resolver and the origin matter.

another approach would be to store and retrieve the "CONF_IPV4_PORT" variable separately. I started doing this but the result was surprisingly ugly. Seems just as good to parse as needed.

Note I have not been able to test this on IPV6 locally as I do not have it. I have assumed that port 53 is the correct default port but some searching is bringing up 5335.

Edit: a bit more searching seems to reveal that 53 is still the right port
Please make and link a doc PR to reflect this adjustment (example).
I wonder if we should add the capability for ipv6 custom port as well in this PR perhaps?

> Please make and link a doc PR to reflect this adjustment (example).

This is done now.

> I wonder if we should add the capability for ipv6 custom port as well in this PR perhaps?

Probably, unfortunately my ISP does not support it, so I wouldn't be able to test IPv6

> > I wonder if we should add the capability for ipv6 custom port as well in this PR perhaps?
> 
> Probably, unfortunately my ISP does not support it, so I wouldn't be able to test IPv6

I can't test either but I still think we should do it.
The typing is different for ipv6 but I think it would be kinda weird to only support custom port for ipv4.

This RFC discusses the proper way(s) if expressing an IPv6 with a port number

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5952#section-6

It seems to prefer the `[address]:port` syntax which will be slightly harder to parse because IPv6 uses colons liberally

Alternatively we could switch to using `address#port` for IPv6 and v4 but this would likely make the feature a bit more "hidden".

review_comments: Should we have a default here too so the user can't leave the field empty and thereby not get a value?

I was following the lead of https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/114058 where defaults were removed here.

Presumably because they were unnecessary duplicates as defaults are defined here: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/113993/files#diff-f7e2ef265b774da4533e59e774aad087920f82fc97c3b9e7801f15537360bb5dR47-R51
You're probably right so let's not have the default in the schema for the options flow. Just have a check so if left empty we set it to `53`.

Isn't that achieved by: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/fabfea5c057d77df97f31a8b691f75cec58a7227/homeassistant/components/dnsip/config_flow.py#L176-L180
As user omitted inputs are replaced by defaults? 

N.B this is not the same as Line 118 which is discussed in the thread above

Tested at [c9e6f5b](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/113993/commits/c9e6f5b1606630cf9338f8588b6ef305ee196ae9)

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/11440490/d6e8585f-edd1-44d5-9427-ab91e70e6935

And this scenario is indeed tested by https://github.com/HarvsG/core/blob/c9e6f5b1606630cf9338f8588b6ef305ee196ae9/tests/components/dnsip/test_config_flow.py#L249
```python
async def test_options_flow_empty_return(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
```
We could just use the same constant right?

We could. I didn't because I couldn't find an RFC that said 53 is definitely the default port for IPV6 and its not a fully implemented standard so I wanted to give scope for things to be easily changed.
That being said, it wouldn't be hard to make the change in the very unlikely event it changes to something other than 53 so I will make your suggested change
